assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Specular reflection
items.clue: Reflection from a smooth surface in a single direction.

items.label: Diffuse reflection
items.clue: Reflection from a rough surface, which causes scattering.

items.label: Absorption
items.clue: The taking in of light energy by a material, so that the light does not leave the material as light.

items.label: Transmission
items.clue: The passing of light through a material, rather than the light being reflected from it or absorbed by it.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the colours of the visible light spectrum?

options.text: Each colour has its own narrow band of wavelength and frequency
Each colour has one exact wavelength and one exact frequency
Each colour has its own wavelength but all share one frequency
All the colours share a wavelength band but differ in speed

questions.explanation: This is the specification statement: every colour occupies a small range of wavelengths together with a matching small range of frequencies.

questions.stem: Red light and violet light both lie within the visible spectrum. Which statement about their bands is correct?

options.text: The red band lies at one fixed wavelength and the violet at another
The red band has longer wavelengths, so it has lower frequencies
The red band has longer wavelengths but the same frequency
The red and violet bands cover the same range of wavelength

questions.explanation: Each colour holds its own band of wavelength and of frequency; red sits at the long-wavelength, low-frequency end of the visible spectrum.

questions.stem: What is the difference between specular reflection and diffuse reflection?

options.text: Specular reflection is from a rough surface, and diffuse from a smooth one
Specular reflection always obeys the law of reflection and diffuse does not
Specular reflection is from a smooth surface, diffuse from a rough one
Specular reflection sends light back and diffuse takes most of it in

questions.explanation: The specification defines specular reflection as reflection from a smooth surface in a single direction, and diffuse reflection as reflection from a rough surface, which scatters the light.

questions.stem: A mirror shows a clear image of a lamp, but a sheet of white paper beside it looks equally bright from every direction. Why does the paper behave differently?

options.text: Its rough surface obeys no law, so the rays leave at random angles
Its rough surface takes in the light and gives it out slowly
Its rough surface transmits light while the mirror reflects it
Its rough surface scatters light into many directions

questions.explanation: Reflection from a rough surface causes scattering — diffuse reflection — so light leaves towards every viewing position and no image is formed.

questions.stem: How does a colour filter work?

options.text: It reflects the unwanted wavelengths and lets the rest through
It absorbs certain wavelengths of light and transmits the others
It adds its own colour to the white light that passes through
It changes the wavelength of the light passing through it

questions.explanation: This is the specification statement: filters work by absorbing certain wavelengths and colours, and transmitting the other wavelengths and colours.

questions.stem: White light is shone through a blue filter. What emerges from the filter, and why?

options.text: All the colours, but with the blue much brighter than the rest
White light that has been dyed blue as it travelled through
Blue light, because the other wavelengths are absorbed by it
Blue light, because the other colours reflect back off it

questions.explanation: White light contains every wavelength; the blue filter absorbs all of them except the blue band, which it transmits.

questions.stem: What determines the colour of an opaque object viewed in white light?

options.text: The wavelengths that the object absorbs most strongly of all
The wavelengths that the object gives out when it is warm
The wavelengths that the object lets through itself
The wavelengths that the object reflects most strongly

questions.explanation: The specification states that the colour of an opaque object is determined by which wavelengths are more strongly reflected; the rest are absorbed.

questions.stem: A jumper appears white when it is lit by white light. What is happening to the light that falls on it?

options.text: All wavelengths are reflected equally
All wavelengths are absorbed equally by it
All wavelengths pass straight through the wool
Only the wavelengths of white are reflected

questions.explanation: The specification states that if all wavelengths are reflected equally the object appears white.

questions.stem: A piece of card looks black in a brightly lit room. Which explanation is correct?

options.text: The light passes straight through the card without stopping
The card reflects every wavelength that falls upon it equally
The card absorbs all of the wavelengths of light that fall on it
The card gives out no light of its own in the lit room

questions.explanation: The specification states that if all wavelengths are absorbed the object appears black, because almost no light is reflected to the eye.

questions.stem: Which statement is true of objects that transmit light?

options.text: They must be colourless as well as see-through
They transmit light only when very smooth
They are either translucent or opaque
They are either transparent or translucent

questions.explanation: This is the specification statement: objects that transmit light are either transparent or translucent.

questions.stem: Frosted bathroom glass lets light into the room, but no clear image can be seen through it. How is the glass best described?

options.text: Translucent, since it scatters the light passing through
Transparent, since the light gets through the glass easily
Opaque, since there is no clear image to be seen through it
Specular, since the rough surface reflects light

questions.explanation: Light is transmitted, so the glass is not opaque, but the scattering destroys the image — which is exactly what translucent means.

questions.stem: A book cover appears red in white light. Which explanation of its colour is correct?

options.text: Red is absorbed by the cover and other wavelengths reflected
Red is reflected and the other wavelengths absorbed
Red is transmitted through the cover and the rest reflected
Red light is given out by the cover in any conditions

questions.explanation: Differential treatment of the wavelengths gives the colour: the red band is reflected most strongly and the wavelengths not reflected are absorbed.
